title: Scaling Backend Systems
speaker: Priya Nair
text: When you're scaling a backend system, the first bottleneck is almost always the database connection pool, not the application code itself.

title: Scaling Backend Systems
speaker: Priya Nair
text: We moved to a hybrid retrieval approach combining keyword search with dense vector embeddings to improve recall on rare technical terms.

title: Intro to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
speaker: David Kim
text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation lets a language model ground its answers in real documents instead of relying purely on parametric memory.

title: Intro to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
speaker: David Kim
text: A cross-encoder reranker looks at the query and each candidate passage together, which makes it far more accurate than embedding similarity alone, but also much slower.

title: Query Understanding and Routing
speaker: Priya Nair
text: Before you retrieve anything, you should classify what kind of question the user is actually asking, because a factual lookup and a summarization request need different pipelines.

title: Query Understanding and Routing
speaker: Priya Nair
text: An intent classifier sitting in front of your retriever can cut wasted retrieval calls dramatically, since not every query needs the heavy hybrid search path.

title: Graph Databases for Metadata
speaker: David Kim
text: Neo4j is useful here because episodes, speakers, and topics naturally form a graph, so you can ask things like which speakers most often discuss retrieval.

title: Graph Databases for Metadata
speaker: David Kim
text: Metadata-aware retrieval means filtering candidate transcript segments by speaker or topic before scoring, which shrinks the search space considerably.

title: Reducing LLM Token Costs
speaker: Priya Nair
text: The cheapest tokens are the ones you never send, so trimming and reranking retrieved passages before they hit the prompt saves real money at scale.

title: Reducing LLM Token Costs
speaker: David Kim
text: We cut our average prompt size by only passing the top reranked passages instead of every retrieved candidate, which reduced token consumption significantly.
